A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGP-GenBench and reinforcement-learning work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the two new appendix experiments in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, RL training results, ablations, and analyses of generated SVG programs, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds CAD-generation experiments and deterministic SVG correctness evaluations in Appendices E.6–E.7.

M1.justification: The SVG GRPO procedure and reward equations remain unchanged. Appendix E.6 adds a CAD-specific adaptation that generates CadQuery Python programs, gates rewards on successful execution, and combines size-normalized geometric IoU with CLIP alignment rewards.

E1.justification: Appendix E.6 extends the work to 3D CAD generation using data assembled from DeepCAD, Text2CAD, and Text2CADQuery. Appendix E.7 adds constrained two-object SVG generation with six explicitly verified spatial relations. Existing SVG datasets remain; SGP-Single-9k becoming SGP-Object is a naming correction.

E2.justification: The new formal comparison in Table 13 evaluates additional comparators: Claude-4-Sonnet, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4, DeepSeek-V3, and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set. Membership in the retained benchmark and ablation tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a deterministic evaluation protocol requiring valid syntax, shape/color object matching, and correct geometric relations, plus a CAD setup using Qwen-2.5-3B and geometric, semantic, and execution-validity measurements. Section 3.1 also changes the reported captioner from Gemini-2.5-Flash-Preview to Gemini-2.0-Flash, matching Appendix A.1 in both versions; this establishes a documentation correction, not recaptioning or rerunning.

E4.justification: Appendix E.7 adds an independent validation addressing evaluation circularity: whether perceptual-reward gains also appear under executable symbolic checks, with per-relation diagnostics. Appendix E.6 adds analysis of CAD reward trajectories and qualitative examples. The earlier reward, CoT, algorithm, data-mixture, and SVG behavior analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 7 retains the same standard-deviation bands and explanation of variability across prompts and sampling replicates. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are introduced; the added experiments report point estimates and training curves.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 13 reports formal pass rates of 41.33% for Qwen-2.5-7B and 72.17% for its RL variant, with Claude-4-Sonnet at 99.50%. Figure 13 and Table 12 add CAD training outcomes and renderings, including reported IoU around 0.35 and CLIP reward around 0.65. These are new experiments, not improvements over v1 under retained settings.

T1.justification: The task formulation, GRPO objective, and reward equations remain mathematically unchanged. The new formal checker is an empirical evaluation procedure; v2 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SGP-GenBench, RL-based SVG improvement, and emergent drawing strategies. The appendix additions supply supporting evidence without redefining those central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly raises potential circularity between vision-based rewards and evaluation, and interprets geometric-checking gains as evidence of formal instruction-following. It also interprets the CAD pilot as support for applicability beyond SVG. Existing discussions of texture difficulty, 3D relations, and limited cross-domain generalization remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.6 documents the approximately 70,000-example CAD dataset, abstract-caption selection, Qwen-2.5-3B backbone, shape normalization, execution requirements, and example generation prompts. E.7 describes object binding and geometric checking. Existing SVG hyperparameters, hardware, framework link, and data-release statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds GenEval as benchmark inspiration and discusses Reason-SVG and rendering-aware RL for vector graphics. Section 7 now explicitly distinguishes the approach from StarVector's paired SVG supervision and image-to-SVG reconstruction. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate citations.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar, spelling, duplicated judge-model text, dataset terminology, and some section headings and affiliations. It expands one related-work passage and adds Appendices E.6–E.7, while retaining the main narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR typography, headers, margins, and front-page formatting. The abstract now fits on the first page, Figure 1 moves to page 2, and numerous existing figures and tables are resized or regrouped across pages. New Figure 13 and Tables 12–13 display the CAD and formal-validation results.

improvement.justification: The independent geometric evaluation adds useful evidence beyond v1's vision-model-based scoring, and the CAD pilot provides empirical support for broader applicability. Captioner consistency and research positioning also improve. The gain remains limited: formal validation covers constrained two-object layouts, while CAD evidence consists mainly of training curves and three examples without a reported held-out quantitative comparison. The central method and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
